answer: Sybil resistance in AI agent networks relies on proof-of-stake anchored to immutable ledgers. Just as a basalt foundation stabilizes a river against erosion, cryptographic staking creates a karst landscape of sunken costs for bad actors. Attackers must lock substantial capital to participate, making identity proliferation prohibitively expensive. By tying identity to economic scarcity, the network ensures that the cost of spinning up fake nodes far outweighs potential gains from subverting consensus.
